newsitem.title: USA: FCC seeks free TV airtime for political candidates.
newsitem.headline: FCC seeks free TV airtime for political candidates.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 24, Reuter - Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said on Tuesday that television companies operating local stations should give free airtime to certain non-Presidential political candidates.
He said he would work to win wide industry agreement on the proposal covering candidates for the U.S. Senate, House of Representatives and state governorships after the U.S. presidential election.

Hundt said during a speech to an industry conference that A.H. Belo Corp, a newspaper and televison company based in Texas, had agreed to give five-minute slots to Senate, House and gubernatorial candidates on its seven stations. The give-away to the non-presidential candidates was the first by a commerical station in the United States, an aide to Hundt said.
"I am applauding it like crazy," Hundt said of the Belo decision. "...And I hope it's contagious."

Hundt told reporters after his speech that he aimed to spur an industry discussion on organizing free airtime for non-presidential candidates, but said he did not believe regulations would be required to get wide adoption by the roughly 1,500 local television stations across the United States.
"I don't think we should start with the assumption of rules," he said.
Political advertising is a major profit source for U.S. broadcasters, giving lifts to industry earnings especially during presidental elections held every four years.
An extended debate on giving free time to presidential candidates was touched off earlier this year by an offer of free time by the Fox network owned by News Corp Ltd.
Belo owns stations in Dallas, Houston, Tulsa, Seattle, New Orleans, Sacramento and Norfolk, Va.
